(1) In November 1993, accounting standards were issued which changed the way companies account for Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOP). The new standard changes the measurement of compensation expense from the cost of the ESOP shares to the fair value of the ESOP shares. To the extent that fair value exceeds cost, this differential is credited to stockholders' equity. The accounting standard is effective for ESOPs created during fiscal years beginning after December 15, 1993. The Company believes that earnings per share information is more relevant when the ESOP fair market value adjustment is eliminated for the following reasons: (i) comparison of the Company's results with those of many other financial institutions is facilitated since companies which established ESOPs during fiscal years prior to December 15, 1993, measure compensation expense based on the original cost of the ESOP shares; and (ii) the ESOP fair market value adjustment is a non-cash charge to earnings with the corresponding credit to stockholders' equity. As such, total stockholders' equity, which defines the Company's capacity for growth, share repurchases and/or payment of dividends is unaffected by the charge.
(2) Due to the Company's conversion to stock ownership on July 2, 1996, per share figures for 1996 are not available. 1%
